confirmed: The GameNative packaged payload is byte-identical to the public wrapper-gamenative-20260719 artifact member, so its build pipeline (GameNative/mesa fork, NDK r29 workflow) is identified.

GameNative/mesa at 5212f63a (wrapper-25, merged 8e64d5f4 two days before the artifact) contains every previously-unidentified wrapper compile unit and the WRAPPER_DIAG code present in the GameNative payload.

The default payload is a debug Termux build of the Pipetto-crypto/mesa fork line: its fork-unique and cache literals match Pipetto sources (90.6%), its physical-device literal matches ac54448c (not e53b3999), and GameNative-only literals are absent.
Neither packaged payload is a build of the reviewed v0.0.5r5 source; they are newer fork-line builds (NDK r29/clang 21, 16KB LOAD alignment, ICD-only 15 exports).
The two packaged variants come from two different (public) forks, not one repository.
open: Exact source commit for the GameNative release artifact is not embedded in the artifact; 5212f63a/8e64d5f4 is the branch state two days before the release, not a recorded build ref.
Exact commit and build record for the default Termux debug build are not in the payload; ac54448c (2026-10-16) is a lower bound supported by literal evidence only.
No attempt was made to build either fork and reproduce the payload bytes (large Mesa build; not needed for the identity claim).
The unwrapped archive metadata/tag names for the release artifacts were not fully enumerated (GitHub release listing returned no entries to the API query used).
limitations: Static analysis of debug strings/ELF sections only; no execution, repackaging, image-quality, concurrency or performance claim.

Literal matching is a fingerprint heuristic: absence of a literal can be caused by dead-code elimination (explains why the stripped GameNative payload matches only ~70% of its source literals); the conclusions rest on fork-unique present/absent patterns and the exact artifact hash match.
Candidate commits are those reachable in the public default branches at hunt time; branches may move.
Raw hunt artifacts are kept outside the repository.
